title: Joining House Flambeau (Gauntlet by combat)
heading: Joining House Flambeau
summary: How a candidate joins House Flambeau: finding a sponsor, a public combat-oriented Gauntlet judged by the sponsor, failure consequences, direct acceptance and the initiation ceremony.
quotes: By the Peripheral Code, an apprentice who fails his Gauntlet three times is given his fourth by a Quaesitor.

title: Tournament Certamen
heading: Certamen
summary: Altered certamen rules used at Flambeau tournaments: single elimination, best of three duels per match, rest periods, and who chooses Technique and Form.
quotes: The winner of two out of three duels within the match proceeds to the next round.
The youngest magus chooses the Form, and the oldest the Technique

title: Forceless Casting
heading: Forceless Casting
summary: Option for a magus to cast a spell deliberately without Penetration so it cannot affect magi with Magic Resistance, useful in tournaments or large-area spells.
quotes: A magus can deliberately ensure the Penetration Total of a spell does not exceed 0.

title: Dimicatio
heading: Dimicatio
summary: Tournament contest in which magi cast real spells at each other using forceless casting while defending with fast-cast defenses; the first spell to reach the opponent's Parma wins.
quotes: The first magus whose spell reaches his opponent's Parma is the winner.

title: Dimicatio in Detail
heading: Dimicatio in Detail
summary: How to play out a dimicatio with the normal combat rules: range, initiative, alternating offensive spells and fast-cast defenses judged by the storyguide.
quotes: Both competitors roll Initiative and the winner casts the first offensive spell.
a fast-cast defense of one-half the level of the incoming spell is usually sufficient

title: Wizards' Melee
heading: Wizards' Melee
summary: A tournament team event where a magus and grogs try to touch the opposing magus with a forceless spell; lists the usual restrictions on ranges, weapons, damage spells and devices.
quotes: Each team consists of one magus and five grogs.
blunted weapons (–3 to Damage)

title: Tournament Prizes
heading: Tournament Prizes
summary: Guidance on the kinds of prizes a tournament host offers, with vis as the simplest.
quotes: a rook (ten pawns) is a moderate prize

title: Wizard's War and the Order
heading: Wizard's War and the Order
summary: Practical rules of Wizard's War under the Code and Peripheral Code: timing of declaration and duration, limits on harming uninvolved magi, covenant sanctuary, renewed declarations and multiple simultaneous wars.
quotes: A Wizard's War must be declared on the night of a full moon.
It then begins at the rise of the following full moon and lasts until the rise of the third full moon.
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages pp.47-48

title: Declaration of War
heading: Declaration of War
summary: Optional ways Tribunals may treat service of a Wizard's War declaration when the recipient is absent: forwarding addresses, representatives, Quaesitor review and Redcap delivery.
quotes: Most Tribunals hold a declaration of war to be duly served if the recipient was present at the covenant and the declaration was nailed to the door of his sanctum.

title: Reasons to Declare Wizard's War
heading: Reasons to Declare Wizard's War
summary: Describes the motives and uses of Wizard's War beyond killing, including harassment, committing otherwise illegal acts, vengeance pledges and enforcing pacts.
quotes: The Code permits combatants to kill one another, but it doesn't require them to do so.

title: Preparing for Wizard's War
heading: Preparing for Wizard's War
summary: Advice on defending against Wizard's War: retreating to the covenant and its Aegis, self-imposed exile, personal refuges, and outside assistance such as Moon Duration spells.
quotes: Especially useful are spells of Moon Duration, which last until both the full moon and the new moon have set.

title: Waging Wizard's War
heading: Waging Wizard's War
summary: Tactics for fighting a Wizard's War: stealth and reconnaissance, the importance of Arcane Connections to Penetration, finding the enemy, and how magical disguise outpaces detection.
quotes: The real value of an Arcane Connection is the bonus it provides to one's Penetration multiplier (see ArM5, page 84).

title: Schools of Magical Combat
heading: Schools of Magical Combat
summary: Introduces the Flambeau idea of a 'school' of magical combat: a named, coherent style combining particular Arts, Abilities and spells.

title: Choosing a School
heading: Choosing a School
summary: How magi pick a combat school to suit their Hermetic Virtues and Flaws, and how Flambeau apprentices have a school chosen for them by their parens.

title: Schools of Magical Combat at a Glance
heading: Schools of Magical Combat at a Glance
summary: Quick-reference table of the six example schools, what each does, and the Virtue recommended for it.
quotes: | The Founder | Attacks using fire                            | Puissant Ignem                                   |

title: The School of the Founder
heading: The School of the Founder
summary: Fire-based combat school: strengths, weaknesses and play advice for a magus who relies on Ignem attacks.
quotes: Ignem spells do excellent damage compared to other spells of similar magnitude.
related: ArM5 p.87 Spell Mastery magic resistance

title: Option: Variant House Benefits
heading: Option: Variant House Benefits
summary: Optional rule restricting the Flambeau free Minor House Virtue to Puissant Art (Ignem or Perdo), with substitutions allowed for the Ramius, Sebastian and Vilano schools.
quotes: This free Virtue must be either Puissant Art (Ignem) or Puissant Art (Perdo).

title: The School of Apromor
heading: The School of Apromor
summary: Perdo-based combat school aimed at damaging opponents directly, with versatile non-damaging uses but heavy demands on Penetration and Spell Mastery.
quotes: Perdo spells usually disregard the target's Soak

title: Enhancing Spell Penetration
heading: Enhancing Spell Penetration
summary: Practical advice for overcoming high Magic Resistance: favor low-level spells, improve Penetration, use Spell Mastery, and add Arcane and sympathetic connections.
quotes: so if one has both a name and a picture of one's target, the multiplier would be x4
related: ArM5 p.84 Arcane and sympathetic connections

title: The School of Boreas
heading: The School of Boreas
summary: Combat school built on the single combination of Perdo Ignem, using cold and darkness; a narrower, cheaper-to-learn alternative to the Apromor and Founder styles.
quotes: The School of Boreas relies on the single Form-Technique combination of Perdo Ignem.

title: The School of Ramius
heading: The School of Ramius
summary: Combat school that bypasses Magic Resistance with mundane weapons backed by defensive magic, including the problem of a magus's own Parma Magica blocking self-targeted spells.
quotes: Spells of Personal Range always bypass the caster's own Magic Resistance (ArM5, page 85), but Touch- and Voice-Range spells are resisted.

title: The Schools of Sebastian
heading: The Schools of Sebastian
summary: A family of minor combat schools that conjure harmful substances with Forms other than Ignem, usually supported by a Magical Focus.
quotes: Most members of the Sebastian family of schools have a Magical Focus (either Major or Minor)

title: Magical Foci for the Schools of Sebastian
heading: Magical Foci for the Schools of Sebastian
summary: Sample Magical Foci by Form suited to the Sebastian schools, with note on which count as Major.
quotes: Except where noted, all of them would count as Minor Magical Foci.

title: The School of Vilano
heading: The School of Vilano
summary: Combat school based on indirect spells that bypass Magic Resistance; notes aiming with Finesse and the double botch risk of aimed spells.
quotes: indirect spells require two stress rolls (one to cast the spell and another to aim it) and therefore have two chances to botch.

title: Indirect Spells from ArM5
heading: Indirect Spells from ArM5
summary: List of core-book spells that can have at least partial effect without penetrating Magic Resistance, with notes on why each works.
quotes: Magic Resistance does not protect against non-magical stone falling due to gravity.

title: House Acclaim
heading: House Acclaim
summary: Flambeau's free Hermetic Reputation measuring prestige: gained through witnessed deeds, lost through inactivity or ignoble acts, never below zero.
quotes: House Acclaim is a free Reputation that every Flambeau magus gains at the start of play.
Loss of House Acclaim is handled by taking away experience points instead of adding them.
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.21 House Acclaim (Bonisagus)

title: Example Acclaim Awards
heading: Example Acclaim Awards
summary: Table of sample experience-point awards and penalties in House Acclaim for tournaments, certamen, Wizard's War, slaying beasts and renegades, and inactivity.

title: Fighting Invisibly
heading: Fighting Invisibly
summary: Rules for what invisibility does in a fight: protection from melee, missiles and targeted spells, Stealth bonuses, surprise attacks, and the limits of invisible weapons.
quotes: During the first round only, the invisible character automatically goes first and gains a +3 Attack bonus

title: Locating an Invisible Character
heading: Locating an Invisible Character
summary: Opposed roll procedure to pinpoint an invisible character well enough to attack or target him, and when location is automatic or needs no roll.
quotes: make an opposed Perception + Awareness roll against the invisible character's Dexterity + Stealth – Encumbrance + Stealth bonus

title: Effects of Invisibility
heading: Effects of Invisibility
summary: Table giving melee Attack, Defense and Stealth bonuses for an invisible character according to how clear the visual signs of presence are.
quotes: Invisibility grants a bonus to melee attack rolls, but not to missile attacks.

title: Invisibility and Group Combat
heading: Invisibility and Group Combat
summary: Invisible characters cannot fight as trained groups; an untrained group with invisible members gains extra botch dice.
quotes: everyone in the group gains an extra botch die per invisible character

title: Effect Modification for Enchanted Items
heading: Effect Modification for Enchanted Items
summary: New enchanting modification, Fast Trigger, which speeds an item effect's Initiative at a cost in effect level.
quotes: The effect gains a +3 Initiative modifier. This adds +5 to the level of the effect.

title: Spell Mastery Special Abilities
heading: Spell Mastery Special Abilities
summary: New Spell Mastery special abilities: Imperturbable Casting, Obfuscated Casting, Precise Casting and Quick Casting.
quotes: Add +1 to the caster's Initiative Total when he casts the Mastered spell.

title: Mercurian Spell Mastery Abilities
heading: Mercurian Spell Mastery Abilities
summary: Exclusive Spell Mastery special abilities available to members of the Cult of Mercury.
quotes: The first time in a session that the caster botches a roll for this spell or fails the casting roll by exactly one point, she gains 5 experience points toward Mastery of this spell.
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages pp.99-100

title: Creo Aquam Guidelines
heading: Creo Aquam Guidelines
summary: New Creo Aquam guideline for creating ice in natural shapes.
quotes: Create ice in a natural shape, such as a floe or icicle.

title: Projectiles and Rego Magic
heading: Projectiles and Rego Magic
summary: Explains three ways Rego magic can attack (propelled, natural motion, and thrown projectiles) and which bypass Magic Resistance, aiming and range rules for thrown projectiles.
quotes: Most projectiles thrown by spells have a range increment of 20 paces.

title: Muto Auram Guidelines
heading: Muto Auram Guidelines
summary: New Muto Auram guidelines for turning a gas into a harmful gas that causes a Light or Medium Wound.
quotes: Transform a gas into a harmful gas causing a Light Wound (Stamina roll against Ease Factor 6 to resist)

title: Perdo Terram Guidelines
heading: Perdo Terram Guidelines
summary: New Perdo Terram guideline for destroying a single aspect of dirt.
quotes: Destroy one aspect of dirt, such as its weight or its cohesiveness

title: Rego Terram Guidelines
heading: Rego Terram Guidelines
summary: New Rego Terram guidelines for throwing stone projectiles, with damage limited by spell level.
quotes: Hurl a stone projectile with enough force to do +5 damage (range increment of 20 paces)

title: Family and Inheritance
heading: Family
summary: How a magus's birth or adoptive family interacts with the Gift and with law: choosing apprentices, and why magi cannot hold feudal land but may inherit other property and have stewards for child heirs.
quotes: Magi may not enter into feudal relationships, and so may not inherit land.

title: Nepotism
heading: Nepotism
summary: Optional use of family members as agents: the player links story events to their fortunes so Bond Maintenance points from adventure experience can be spent on them.
quotes: This allows the magus to spend Bond Maintenance points, which equal the Adventure experience they receive for the story, on their family members.

title: Family Reputation
heading: Family Reputation
summary: Families carry shared Reputations that characters may use instead of their own among strangers, shaped by every family member's actions.
quotes: characters may use this Reputation instead of their own, among people who do not personally know the character

title: Interference With the Mundanes
heading: Interference With the Mundanes
summary: List of activities that in most Tribunals, and especially where Jerbiton magi are active, are not treated as breaking the Code's ban on interfering with mundanes.
quotes: Be identified as a magus, or cast spells before witnesses, provided this doesn't provoke the mundanes.

title: Etiquette Performances
heading: Etiquette
summary: Introduces etiquette as symbolic communication at events and the three kinds of performance a character can attempt; an observer can tell which kind is being attempted with a roll.
quotes: an Intelligence + Etiquette roll against an Ease Factor of 3

title: Individual Etiquette
heading: Individual
summary: Communication + Etiquette roll against a host-set Ease Factor to be the most memorable attendee at an event and earn Reputation experience; results can be given to another person.
quotes: A character wishing to make an individual impression at an event makes a Communication + Etiquette roll.
At minimum this is 6, but can be as high as 21.

title: Competitive Etiquette (Etiquette Duels)
heading: Competitive
summary: Etiquette duel in which each rival chooses a self-inflicted penalty to impose on both Communication + Etiquette rolls, then results are compared to see who looks boorish or wins the exchange.
quotes: A participant cannot choose a penalty greater than his Etiquette score.
The sum of both selected penalties is subtracted from the standard Etiquette roll of both individuals.

title: Collaborative Etiquette
heading: Collaborative
summary: Group etiquette where participants' rolls are summed into a score compared with past events, with penalties for botches and sample scores for Tribunal feasts, Primus elections and symposia.
quotes: the rolls of all participants are added together
A person who botches during such an event reduces the score by 10, and may develop a poor Reputation.

title: Money and Good Manners
heading: Money and Good Manners
summary: Rules for boosting an Etiquette roll by spending money or by giving suitable gifts, and a roll to learn what gifts a particular magus would value.
quotes: The bonus is equal to +1 for each time the character spends the weekly income of all of his guests.
A character cannot gain a bonus higher than his Etiquette score by spending money.
An Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore + Reputation (of the receiver) roll against an Ease Factor of

title: Hermetic Courtesy and Hospitality
heading: Hermetic Courtesy and Hospitality
summary: Jerbiton code of conduct listing the obligations of guests and hosts when visiting another Jerbiton magus's territory; breaking it is taken as a deliberate insult.
quotes: It is rude to refuse to offer hospitality, but it is also rude to demand it.

title: Electing the Primus (Jerbiton)
heading: Electing the Primus
summary: Procedure for choosing and dismissing the Jerbiton Primus: nomination, hourly ballots eliminating the lowest candidate, proxies, and a petition of one-third of the House to dismiss.
quotes: A maximum of fourteen hourly ballots are taken in a day.
The Primus can be dismissed by one-third of the members of the House requesting that he resign.

title: Rhaetian
heading: Rhaetian
summary: Language note: how well a Rhaetian speaker and a Latin speaker understand each other, based on Rhaetian score.
quotes: A character with a score of 5 in Rhaetian can speak to a person who knows Latin as if he had a score of 2 in that language

title: League Membership
heading: League Membership
summary: Explains Jerbiton leagues, the interest-based clubs most Jerbiton magi belong to, and how they accept other-House members and fit into saga pacing.

title: Designing a League
heading: Designing a League
summary: Options a troupe can choose when building a league: desired stories, senior connections, headquarters, a shared Reputation bonus, assistance and a name, with a worked example.
quotes: All Reputations act as if they were 3 points higher, between colleagues.

title: Less Intelligent Magi?
heading: Less Intelligent Magi?
summary: Optional character-creation note allowing Jerbiton magi with a Gentle Gift and a lower than usual Intelligence in sagas where the Gift is rare.
quotes: An Intelligence score less than +3 reflects a premium placed upon Gentle Giftedness by masters in House Jerbiton.

title: Free Virtue (Jerbiton)
heading: Free Virtue
summary: Jerbiton magi choose their own free House Virtue, limited to Minor Virtues relating to scholarship, art or dealing with people; includes suggested Virtues and Abilities and a ruling on Ability-linked Virtues.
quotes: This choice is limited to Minor Virtues that relate to scholarship, art, or interacting with people.
the magus does not lose this advantage when the Ability is used on non-mundane people
